resources.string: VEX IS HOME · CENTER = CURRENT CONTEXT
Sample preview only. This body is intentionally light while the reusable Android element, placement, navigation, and logging foundations are being learned.
External information will appear here as stable chronological event rows.
Handled this lab: %1$d acknowledged · %2$d later · %3$d suspended · %4$d suppressed
Why: retained oldest unhandled event; its row is visible and no other transient is blocking it.
Acknowledge → keep the row, mark ACKNOWLEDGED, then advance to the next queued candidate (or close if none).
Later → keep the row and move it into the next sequence. The current queue continues first; when it drains, deferred items become eligible.
Suspend → keep the row active but move it behind unsuspended items in the current queue.
Suppress → keep the row, mark SUPPRESSED for this lab session, and remove it from proactive attention until Reset lab.
If the stated next state does not happen, treat it as a failing case / bug.
Future home for preferences, device posture, and user-controlled configuration. This is placeholder content for the first navigation practicum.
Small persisted profile proof. Edit the draft name and save; the persisted field below updates from the repository database flow.
A future VexStream Music connection can live behind this screen without changing Home navigation. For now this screen proves scoped feature actions and a stable destination.
A future conversational Vex runtime can attach here. For now this screen proves that its semantic action stays owned beside the feature instead of moving into the app root.
Run Talk to Vex placeholder action
Reset clears the persisted Log History. New actions begin a fresh history immediately after.

Debug fixture only. Timer tests outside-screen arrival. Emit next is immediate. Burst fills enough rows to scroll. Insert older changes list order without changing existing IDs. Remove oldest tests provider-removal candidate advancement.

Reset lab → choose Rotation or Random → Next expectation → open Events. The popup names the scenario, seed, target position, preferred placement, queue counts, and expected button results. Rotation cycles top, middle, bottom, then blocking-freeze. Random is seeded and replayable. If the stated next state does not happen, that is a bug.
Placement expectation: prefer %1$s; safe fallback is allowed when geometry cannot fit it.
BLOCKING: displayed list is frozen at scenario entry while provider truth may keep advancing. Acknowledge must release the freeze and reveal accumulated provider rows.
Rotation: top+Acknowledge → middle+Later → bottom+Suspend → middle+Suppress → blocking+Acknowledge → repeat.
Random mode is deterministic for the displayed seed; reuse that seed to reproduce the same scenario sequence.
Reusable cells used by this first Android construction practicum.
Two local presentation styles using the same open/close ownership rules.
AlertDialog remains available as a centered blocking modal pattern.
ModalBottomSheet is suited to draggable, vertically spacious content and can be dismissed by dragging down.
Container and row compose smaller cells without changing their identities.
Registered topology. Open a row to move one layer deeper without flattening the whole app into one map.
